lead: No natural product reaches grade A for major depressive disorder (depression), but many have randomized trials. A review of 35 trials in 6,993 people found more people responded to St John's wort than to placebo, with no difference from antidepressants in mild and moderate depression, although results varied a lot between trials (grade B); St John's wort can also weaken many prescription medicines and has caused serotonin syndrome when combined with antidepressants. Depression is treatable; anyone with thoughts of self-harm should contact a doctor or a crisis line straight away.

grade_key.A: Meta-analysis, or at least 2 randomized trials with low risk of bias and a consistent benefit
grade_key.B: 1 good randomized trial, or several randomized trials with mixed results
grade_key.C: Observational studies, small pilots or open-label trials only
grade_key.Negative: Randomized trials found no benefit over placebo

disclaimer: This page summarizes published research. It is not medical advice. Talk to a clinician before starting any supplement, especially if you take other medicines.

products.name: Acetyl-L-carnitine
products.summary: A 2018 meta-analysis of 12 randomized trials in 791 participants (11 tested acetyl-L-carnitine on its own) found that it reduced depressive symptoms compared with placebo or no intervention across nine trials, with results that varied widely between trials, and found similar effectiveness to antidepressants in three trials. The effect appeared strongest in older adults, and the authors said large trials are needed to confirm or refute the findings. The abstract does not say how depression was diagnosed in the included trials.
products.safety_interactions: In the three trials comparing acetyl-L-carnitine with antidepressants, the rate of adverse effects was significantly lower with acetyl-L-carnitine. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: L-carnitine and acetyl-L-carnitine
general_safety.short: In neuropathy trials, adverse events with acetyl-L-carnitine were similar to placebo; L-carnitine taken for 12 to 24 weeks raised blood TMAO, a compound linked to atherosclerosis.

citations.label: Veronese et al., 2018, Psychosom Med
citations.title: Acetyl-L-Carnitine Supplementation and the Treatment of Depressive Symptoms: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

products.name: Creatine
products.summary: Creatine has been tested as an addition to other treatment. In an 8-week double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 52 women with major depressive disorder, creatine (5 g a day) added to escitalopram gave significantly greater improvement in depression scores than placebo added to escitalopram. A 2026 systematic review of 5 randomized trials (4 in major depressive disorder) also reported a benefit when creatine was added to cognitive behavioural therapy and no difference from placebo in a trial in female adolescents. A 2025 meta-analysis of 11 trials in 1,093 people with or without depression found a small average effect that was not clinically important, with very low quality evidence and signs of bias favouring creatine.
products.safety_interactions: In the 52-person trial the overall frequency of adverse events was similar with creatine and placebo. The 2026 review described creatine as generally well tolerated and noted hypomania or mania in two of 17 participants given creatine. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: Creatine
general_safety.short: Creatine is associated with a small rise in blood creatinine, described as transient, without a significant change in kidney filtration; no serious adverse outcomes in studies of women.

products.name: Curcumin
products.summary: A 2020 meta-analysis (10 studies, 531 participants; in 7 of the 9 articles participants had major depressive disorder) found an overall significant effect of curcumin on depressive symptoms and suggested it might help when added to standard care, while warning that the small sample means the results should be interpreted cautiously. A 2021 meta-analysis of 10 trials in 594 patients found a smaller effect, judged three trials at high risk of bias and four unclear, and rated the evidence quality low, indicating great uncertainty.
products.safety_interactions: The 2020 meta-analysis reported that curcumin was generally well tolerated. The 2021 meta-analysis found no difference from control in dropout rates or in digestive or neurological symptoms. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: Turmeric and curcumin
general_safety.short: Case series link turmeric supplements to liver injury, sometimes severe. Curcumin may alter levels of some drugs, including anticoagulants, mostly in non-clinical studies.

citations.title: Curcumin for depression: a meta-analysis.

citations.label: Wang et al., 2021, J Affect Disord
citations.title: The efficacy and acceptability of curcumin for the treatment of depression or depressive symptoms: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

products.name: Folate, L-methylfolate and vitamin B12
products.summary: These have been tested almost entirely as add-ons to antidepressants: a 2018 meta-analysis in unipolar depression found no trials of folate or methylfolate alone against placebo. A 2022 meta-analysis found a small benefit when L-methylfolate was added to an antidepressant in adults with major depressive disorder (3 studies, 483 people). The 2018 meta-analysis found a significant benefit only for folate below 5 mg a day or methylfolate 15 mg a day added to an SSRI, and graded all the evidence low or very low quality. A 2016 meta-analysis of folic acid added to antidepressants found no significant difference from placebo. A 2015 meta-analysis found that short-term folate and vitamin B12 did not improve symptoms in adults with major depression treated with antidepressants, though longer use may lower the risk of relapse. A 2021 meta-analysis of 16 trials found no overall effect of vitamin B12 or B-complex on measures of depression; its participants were not selected for diagnosed depression.
products.safety_interactions: A 2016 review of nutrients added to antidepressants noted no major adverse effects in the studies apart from minor digestive disturbance. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: B vitamins
general_safety.short: High vitamin B6 levels, usually from supplements, may cause sensory nerve damage. Folic acid did not change cancer rates over about 5 years in large trials.

products.name: Lavender oil (taken by mouth)
products.summary: One randomized, double-blind, placebo- and reference-controlled trial tested a lavender oil preparation taken by mouth (80 mg a day) on its own for 8 weeks in 498 people with a mild or moderate episode of major depressive disorder. Depression scores fell 2.17 points more with lavender oil than with placebo on the Montgomery Asberg scale, and 2.59 points more with the reference antidepressant sertraline than with placebo. A second 2026 paper analyses individual symptoms in the same trial. The finding rests on a single trial.
products.safety_interactions: The trial reported that the lavender oil preparation was well tolerated and that eructation (belching) was its most frequent adverse effect. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: Lavender
general_safety.short: A large review found a safe profile in trials but poor safety reporting. Case reports link continuous use of lavender-fragranced products to breast growth in young children, reversing on stopping.

products.name: Magnesium
products.summary: A 2023 meta-analysis of 7 placebo-controlled trials in 325 adults with depressive disorder found a significant fall in depression scores with magnesium and called for high-quality trials with larger samples. Individual trials disagree. In a double-blind trial of 37 people with recurrent depressive disorder, magnesium added to fluoxetine made no significant difference to depression scores compared with placebo added to fluoxetine. In a double-blind trial in depressed patients with magnesium deficiency, scores fell more with magnesium oxide than with placebo. An open-label randomized cross-over trial in 126 adults with mild-to-moderate symptoms found improvement after 6 weeks of magnesium chloride (248 mg of elemental magnesium a day), but it was compared with no treatment rather than placebo.
products.safety_interactions: In the open-label trial of magnesium chloride the supplements were reported to be well tolerated. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: Magnesium
general_safety.short: Oral magnesium mainly causes gastrointestinal effects such as diarrhoea; severe high blood magnesium occurs almost only in people with substantially reduced kidney function.

products.name: N-acetylcysteine (NAC)
products.summary: N-acetylcysteine has been tested as an add-on treatment, and the meta-analyses mix people with major depressive disorder and bipolar depression. A 2020 meta-analysis of 7 double-blind placebo-controlled trials in bipolar depression and major depressive disorder found that it did not improve depressive symptoms compared with placebo. A 2024 meta-analysis of 12 studies in 904 patients found a small significant difference in favour of N-acetylcysteine, particularly in bipolar disorder, and said large trials were needed. In a 2016 meta-analysis of 5 studies that found a benefit, only 1 study enrolled people with major depressive disorder in a current episode.
products.safety_interactions: The 2020 meta-analysis found more gastrointestinal adverse events with N-acetylcysteine than with placebo. The 2016 meta-analysis reported only minor adverse events. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: N-acetylcysteine (NAC)
general_safety.short: In a review of 41 reports in chronic lung disease, stomach and bowel symptoms occurred but were no more common than in control groups, including at higher doses.

products.name: Omega-3 fatty acids
products.summary: A 2021 Cochrane review in adults with major depressive disorder pooled 33 placebo-controlled studies with 1,848 people and found a small to modest reduction in depressive symptoms that it judged unlikely to be clinically meaningful, with very low-certainty evidence and no difference in remission or response rates. A 2019 meta-analysis of 26 double-blind trials in 2,160 people found a benefit with formulations that were mostly EPA but not with those that were mostly DHA. A 2025 meta-analysis of 36 studies found a small overall effect, with significant heterogeneity and publication bias and no advantage over placebo in response or remission. Added to an antidepressant, a 2016 meta-analysis found a moderate to strong effect but signs of study bias. In children and adolescents, a 2024 Cochrane review of 5 trials in 228 participants found the evidence very uncertain.
products.safety_interactions: In the 2021 Cochrane review the number of people with adverse events was similar with omega-3 and placebo, though the estimate was imprecise. In the review of children and adolescents no serious adverse effects were reported, and one study reported more muscle cramps in the fish oil group. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: Omega-3 fatty acids
general_safety.short: Linked to a higher risk of atrial fibrillation in cardiovascular trials, more so above 1 g/day; diarrhoea and altered taste were more likely than with placebo; bleeding findings are mixed.

products.name: Probiotics
products.summary: A 2025 meta-analysis of randomized trials in clinically diagnosed samples (23 trials, 1,401 patients; 18 trials tested probiotics for depression) found a significant reduction in depression symptoms with probiotics, with high heterogeneity between studies; prebiotics showed no significant effect. A second 2025 meta-analysis of 7 randomized trials in patients with depression also found fewer depressive symptoms with probiotics than with placebo. A 2025 network meta-analysis in adults with major depressive disorder, covering 42 placebo-controlled trials of antidepressants and of probiotics, prebiotics or synbiotics, rated the certainty of evidence moderate to very low and noted a lack of head-to-head trials between probiotics and antidepressants. Strains, doses and whether probiotics were used alone or with an antidepressant differ between trials.
products.safety_interactions: The network meta-analysis reported that longer-term probiotic use showed the same tolerability as antidepressants. Specific adverse events and interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited abstracts.

general_safety.name: Probiotics
general_safety.short: Trials have not shown increased risk, though safety reporting is weak. Rare bloodstream infections occur, mainly in people who are severely ill, immunosuppressed or in intensive care.

products.name: Probiotics with magnesium orotate and coenzyme Q10
products.summary: One randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial tested this combination in 120 adults diagnosed with major depressive disorder for 8 weeks. Fewer people in the combination group still had a major depressive episode at the end of treatment, but depressive symptom measures differed from placebo only at 4 weeks, not at 8 or 16 weeks. Because the ingredients were given together, the trial cannot show what any one of them does. Graded B because this was a double-blind placebo-controlled randomised trial in adults diagnosed with depression; it is a single trial with mixed outcomes.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Probiotics
general_safety.short: Trials have not shown increased risk, though safety reporting is weak. Rare bloodstream infections occur, mainly in people who are severely ill, immunosuppressed or in intensive care.

general_safety.name: Magnesium
general_safety.short: Oral magnesium mainly causes gastrointestinal effects such as diarrhoea; severe high blood magnesium occurs almost only in people with substantially reduced kidney function.

general_safety.name: Coenzyme Q10
general_safety.short: Few adverse events were reported in trials. A case report describes reduced warfarin response while taking CoQ10.

citations.label: Strodl et al., 2024, Sci Rep
citations.title: Probiotics and magnesium orotate for the treatment of major depressive disorder: a randomised double blind controlled trial.

products.name: Rhodiola
products.summary: Three randomized trials give mixed results. In a 12-week placebo-controlled trial, 57 people with mild to moderate major depressive disorder received rhodiola extract, sertraline or placebo; there was no significant difference between the groups. In a 6-week double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 89 people with mild to moderate depression, depression scores improved significantly within the two rhodiola groups and not within the placebo group (a within-group change). In a 12-week double-blind trial in 100 people, depression scores fell more when rhodiola at 0.6 g a day was added to sertraline than with sertraline and placebo.
products.safety_interactions: In the 57-person trial, fewer people reported adverse events with rhodiola (30.0%) than with sertraline (63.2%); the placebo figure was 16.7%. The 6-week trial reported no serious side effects in any group. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: Rhodiola
general_safety.short: Appeared well tolerated in short-term studies. A volunteer study found modest CYP2C9 inhibition (possibly relevant to warfarin, phenytoin); one case report of serotonergic symptoms with paroxetine.

products.name: S-adenosylmethionine (SAMe)
products.summary: A 2016 Cochrane review of 8 randomized trials in adults diagnosed with major depression, which accepted both oral and injected SAMe, found no strong evidence that SAMe on its own differed from placebo (2 studies, very low quality evidence). Added to an SSRI antidepressant, SAMe was superior to placebo in one study of 73 people (low quality evidence). A 2024 meta-analysis of 14 trials in 1,522 people found no significant difference between SAMe and placebo, either alone or as an add-on. In a 12-week double-blind analysis of 144 adults with major depressive disorder (a subsample from one site of a two-site study), SAMe at 1600 to 3200 mg a day improved depression scores more than placebo, while the comparison antidepressant did not separate from placebo. The same abstract notes that the full two-site study showed no significant difference between groups, because of site differences, and calls the single-site results preliminary.
products.safety_interactions: The Cochrane review noted that specific adverse effects were not detailed in most studies and recorded two reports of mania or hypomania among 441 participants given SAMe. A 2018 case report describes mania with psychotic features in a person taking SAMe together with an SSRI antidepressant. Other interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: S-adenosylmethionine (SAMe)
general_safety.short: Dropout rates in depression trials were similar to placebo or antidepressants. A review says it is contraindicated in bipolar disorder; a case report describes mania with an SSRI.

products.name: Saffron
products.summary: A 2026 meta-analysis of 34 randomized trials in 1,769 adults found lower scores on a self-rated depression scale with saffron (14 trials, 817 people) but no significant effect on the clinician-rated Hamilton scale; it rated the certainty of evidence moderate, and its abstract does not say how many participants had diagnosed depression. A 2019 meta-analysis limited to people with mild to moderate depression pooled nine trials and found saffron more effective than placebo. A 2013 meta-analysis in adults with major depressive disorder included only 5 trials and called for larger trials by research teams outside Iran. Compared directly with SSRI antidepressants in 8 trials, saffron showed no significant difference in depressive symptoms; that comparison does not show that saffron can replace prescribed treatment.
products.safety_interactions: A 2020 meta-analysis of 12 studies found no significant difference in the rate of adverse effects between saffron and placebo or between saffron and antidepressants. A 2025 meta-analysis found fewer adverse events with saffron than with SSRIs. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: Saffron
general_safety.short: In a meta-analysis of 12 depression studies, adverse effects were no more common than with placebo. In a 1-week volunteer study the higher dose lowered standing blood pressure.

products.name: St John's wort
products.summary: Studied on its own, not added to an antidepressant. A 2008 Cochrane review of 29 randomized double-blind trials in 5,489 people with major depression found more responders with hypericum extracts than with placebo, but the placebo-controlled results varied markedly: the response rate ratio was 1.28 in nine larger trials and 1.87 in nine smaller ones, and trials from German-speaking countries were more favourable. A 2016 review of 35 randomized trials in 6,993 adults with major depressive disorder found St John's wort superior to placebo and not significantly different from antidepressant medication in mild and moderate depression (moderate quality of evidence), and noted that heterogeneity and a lack of research in severe depression reduce the quality of the evidence. A 2026 network meta-analysis of nutraceutical trials in major depressive disorder rated its confidence in the evidence low to very low.
products.safety_interactions: In the trials, fewer people stopped St John's wort because of adverse effects than stopped older antidepressants, and adverse events were comparable to placebo; the 2016 review cautioned that adverse events were poorly reported and that the trials were not designed to detect rare events. Reviews of drug interactions report that St John's wort lowers the blood level or effect of many medicines, including warfarin, cyclosporin, digoxin, HIV medicines and oral contraceptives (with unwanted pregnancies reported), probably by inducing cytochrome P450 enzymes and P-glycoprotein. They also report serotonin syndrome when St John's wort was taken with serotonin reuptake inhibitor antidepressants, and describe some interactions as life-threatening.

general_safety.name: St John's wort
general_safety.short: Induces drug-metabolising enzymes and lowers levels or effect of many medicines (e.g. warfarin, cyclosporin, digoxin, oral contraceptives). Serotonin syndrome reported with SSRI antidepressants.

products.name: Vitamin D
products.summary: A 2019 meta-analysis of 4 randomized trials in 948 people with clinically diagnosed major depression (vitamin D was given by mouth in three and by injection in one) found a moderate improvement in depression ratings and called the finding tentative because of the small number of trials and methodological bias in some. A 2023 meta-analysis of 18 placebo-controlled trials in 1,980 depressed patients found vitamin D superior to placebo, with results that varied widely between trials and a benefit in adults but not in children and adolescents; some trials gave intermittent high doses by mouth or a single high dose by injection into muscle; concurrent antidepressant use did not change the effect. A 2024 meta-analysis of 18 trials in adults with primary depression found a small overall effect and none in people whose vitamin D level was below 50 nmol/L. A 2026 network meta-analysis described the pooled effect of vitamin D3 in its low risk-of-bias analysis as higher than expected or unrealistic and rated confidence in the evidence low to very low.
products.safety_interactions: The 2023 meta-analysis found similar dropout rates with vitamin D and placebo. The cited abstracts do not describe adverse events or interactions with medicines.

general_safety.name: Vitamin D
general_safety.short: Long-term supplementation raised the risk of high blood calcium and high urine calcium in trials, but not kidney stones; toxicity from extremely high doses is rare but serious.

products.name: Zinc
products.summary: A 2021 meta-analysis pooled 5 randomized trials of zinc added to antidepressant drugs in people with clinical depression and found a modest reduction in depressive symptoms compared with placebo, though the effect was not significant when trials were grouped by sample size. A 2022 meta-analysis of randomized trials found lower depression scores with zinc in depressed patients, but only when zinc was given on its own, and called for further trials of zinc alone versus added to other treatment. A 2016 review of nutrients added to antidepressants described the results for zinc as mixed.
products.safety_interactions: A 2016 review of nutrients added to antidepressants, which included zinc, noted no major adverse effects in the studies apart from minor digestive disturbance. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: Zinc
general_safety.short: Nausea and bad taste were more common with zinc in common-cold trials. Case reports link zinc supplements and zinc overload to copper deficiency, causing anaemia or nerve damage.

products.name: 5-HTP (5-hydroxytryptophan)
products.summary: A 2020 systematic review found 13 studies of 5-HTP in depressed patients and pooled 7; depression scores improved, but results varied widely and the reviewers judged the studies relatively weak because few included placebo groups, so most of the pooled result is a within-group change. A Cochrane review of tryptophan and 5-HTP found only two trials of sufficient quality, with 64 patients in total (one of them tested 5-HTP), and considered the evidence of insufficient quality to be conclusive. Graded C because almost none of the evidence is placebo-controlled.
products.safety_interactions: The cited abstracts give no adverse-event findings. A 2006 review states that it covers safety issues with 5-HTP, with emphasis on eosinophilia myalgia syndrome and serotonin syndrome, but its abstract reports no results. A Cochrane review of tryptophan and 5-HTP noted that a possible link between these substances and the potentially fatal eosinophilia-myalgia syndrome has not been resolved.

general_safety.name: 5-HTP (5-hydroxytryptophan)
general_safety.short: A safety review found no definitive toxicity cases in 20 years of use; a link to eosinophilia-myalgia syndrome is unresolved. One case report of serotonin syndrome with linezolid.

citations.title: Serotonin a la carte: supplementation with the serotonin precursor 5-hydroxytryptophan.

products.name: Ashwagandha with piperine
products.summary: One randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial tested ashwagandha root extract with piperine (500 mg with 5 mg) for 90 days in 70 people with mild to moderate depression and anxiety; depression and anxiety improved in both groups and improved significantly more with the extract. The abstract does not say how depression was diagnosed, and no trial of ashwagandha alone in people diagnosed with major depressive disorder was found in a PubMed search on 25 November 2026. A 2026 meta-analysis of 22 trials in adults reported improved depression scores, but its abstract does not say the participants had diagnosed depression, and it called for high-quality trials to address heterogeneity. Graded C because the one trial found in depressed people is small and tested a combination.
products.safety_interactions: In the 70-person trial, blood test results stayed in the normal range and the extract was reported to be well tolerated. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: Ashwagandha
general_safety.short: Case reports link ashwagandha to liver injury (jaundice, itching), with deaths in people who already had cirrhosis, and to thyrotoxicosis in one reported case.

citations.label: Majeed et al., 2024, J Integr Complement Med
citations.title: A Standardized Withania somnifera (Linn.) Root Extract with Piperine Alleviates the Symptoms of Anxiety and Depression by Increasing Serotonin Levels: A Double-Blind, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Study.

citations.label: Alsanie et al., 2026, Complement Ther Med
citations.title: Effects of ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) on mental health in adults: A systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

products.name: Ginkgo biloba
products.summary: A 2024 meta-analysis of 21 articles in 2,074 patients with depression found lower Hamilton depression scores with ginkgo than in control groups at 4, 6 and 8 weeks. Its outcomes included stroke and daily-living scales, which suggests that many of the trials were in depression after stroke rather than major depressive disorder; the abstract does not describe the trial designs, the control treatments or the risk of bias. No randomized trial of ginkgo in people diagnosed with major depressive disorder was found in a PubMed search on 25 November 2026. Graded C for those reasons.
products.safety_interactions: The meta-analysis found no differences in adverse events between ginkgo and control groups. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: Ginkgo biloba
general_safety.short: Trials of clotting measures indicate no higher bleeding risk, but case reports describe bleeding, including intracranial. Interactions with anticoagulant or antiplatelet medicines cannot be ruled out.

citations.label: Lin et al., 2024, Front Pharmacol
citations.title: Effects and safety of Ginkgo biloba on depression: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

products.name: L-theanine
products.summary: The studies found in this search tested L-theanine as an addition to other treatment. In a six-week randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial, 60 people with major depressive disorder received sertraline plus either L-theanine (200 mg a day) or placebo; depression scores fell more with L-theanine, and response and remission rates at week 6 were higher. The authors named the small sample and short study period as limitations. In an 8-week open-label study, 20 people with major depressive disorder had lower depression scores after L-theanine was added to their current medication (a within-group change with no placebo group). Graded C because the one placebo-controlled trial found is small and short.
products.safety_interactions: In the 60-person trial the frequency of side effects was comparable between L-theanine and placebo. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: L-theanine
general_safety.short: In a meta-analysis of 31 randomised trials (1168 people), no serious adverse events were reported. Small add-on trials with sertraline or risperidone found side effects similar to placebo.

citations.label: Shamabadi et al., 2023, J Affect Disord
citations.title: l-theanine adjunct to sertraline for major depressive disorder: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial.

citations.label: Hidese et al., 2017, Acta Neuropsychiatr
citations.title: Effects of chronic l-theanine administration in patients with major depressive disorder: an open-label study.

products.name: Tryptophan
products.summary: A Cochrane review of tryptophan and 5-HTP located 108 trials but judged only two, with 64 patients in total, to be of sufficient quality (one of them tested L-tryptophan); those two suggested the substances were better than placebo, and the reviewers considered the evidence of insufficient quality to be conclusive. In a double-blind trial in older hospital patients with mild to moderate depression, 6 grams of L-tryptophan a day was no different from placebo over six weeks. In a randomized double-blind trial of 30 people with major depressive disorder, tryptophan added to fluoxetine lowered depression scores more than placebo in the first week only. Graded C because the placebo-controlled trials are small and mostly old and their results conflict.
products.safety_interactions: In the 30-person trial of tryptophan added to fluoxetine, no cases of serotonin syndrome occurred and the combination was well tolerated, although the 4 g a day dose caused daytime drowsiness. A Cochrane review of tryptophan and 5-HTP noted that a possible link between these substances and the potentially fatal eosinophilia-myalgia syndrome has not been resolved.

general_safety.name: Tryptophan
general_safety.short: Occasional tremor, nausea and dizziness, mainly at higher doses; rare serotonin syndrome with serotonergic medicines. A 1989 eosinophilia-myalgia outbreak was linked to contaminated supplements.

products.name: Chromium
products.summary: The randomized trials found in this search tested chromium picolinate in atypical depression. In a double-blind placebo-controlled pilot study in 15 people with major depressive disorder, atypical type, 7 of 10 people given chromium picolinate and none given placebo met responder criteria. A double-blind multicentre replication study then randomized 113 adult outpatients with atypical depression and found no significant difference between chromium and placebo on the primary efficacy measures; a supplemental analysis of 41 people with high carbohydrate craving favoured chromium. Graded Negative because the larger trial found no benefit on its primary measures.
products.safety_interactions: Both trials reported that chromium picolinate was well tolerated. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: Chromium
general_safety.short: In a meta-analysis of 25 diabetes trials, adverse events were no more common than with placebo. One case report describes kidney failure and liver dysfunction after months of excess intake.

citations.label: Docherty et al., 2005, J Psychiatr Pract
citations.title: A double-blind, placebo-controlled, exploratory trial of chromium picolinate in atypical depression: effect on carbohydrate craving.

citations.label: Davidson et al., 2003, Biol Psychiatry
citations.title: Effectiveness of chromium in atypical depression: a placebo-controlled trial.

products.name: Inositol
products.summary: A Cochrane review of 4 short double-blind trials in 141 people with depressive disorders, testing inositol alone or added to other treatment, found no clear evidence of a therapeutic benefit. A 2014 meta-analysis of 7 randomized trials in depression (including bipolar depression, major depressive disorder and premenstrual dysphoric disorder) found no statistically significant effect on depressive symptoms. In a controlled double-blind trial, adding inositol did not improve depression in people who had not responded to an SSRI antidepressant.
products.safety_interactions: The Cochrane review found no evidence of poor acceptability. In the 2014 meta-analysis, gastrointestinal upset was marginally more common with inositol than with placebo. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: Inositol
general_safety.short: A safety review found only mild nausea, flatus and diarrhoea at the highest dose studied (12 g/day). In an uncontrolled 15-person pilot, an inositol blend did not disrupt lithium or valproate therapy.

citations.title: Inositol for depressive disorders.

citations.label: Mukai et al., 2014, Hum Psychopharmacol
citations.title: A meta-analysis of inositol for depression and anxiety disorders.

citations.label: Nemets et al., 1999, J Neural Transm (Vienna)
citations.title: Inositol addition does not improve depression in SSRI treatment failures.

products.name: Melatonin
products.summary: A 2022 meta-analysis of 19 studies in 1,178 patients, covering both primary and secondary depression symptoms, found that melatonin was not significantly beneficial for depressive symptoms overall. A 2014 systematic review of 10 studies in 486 patients, only two of them in patients with depression, found no significant effect in its two meta-analyses. In a small double-blind trial in major depressive disorder, 10 people given slow-release melatonin with fluoxetine slept better than 9 given placebo with fluoxetine, but melatonin had no effect on the rate of improvement in depression.
products.safety_interactions: The 2014 review reported no serious adverse events. In the trial with fluoxetine, no particular side effects were noted from the combination. Other interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: Melatonin
general_safety.short: Trial adverse events were few and mostly mild (daytime sleepiness, headache, dizziness); long-term data are limited. Drugs acting on CYP1A2 may slow its breakdown.

citations.title: Melatonin for the treatment of sleep disturbances in major depressive disorder.

products.name: Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10)
products.summary: Two recent meta-analyses pooled small randomized trials of CoQ10 and depressive symptoms, but most of the trials were not in people with major depressive disorder. In one, of 5 trials in 474 people, three enrolled people whose depression accompanied multiple sclerosis, breast cancer or polycystic ovary syndrome, and two enrolled people with primary depressive disorders (major depression and bipolar disorder). The other, of seven small trials across different clinical populations, found an effect on one rating scale but not on another and concluded that more data are needed. This is too little evidence in major depressive disorder itself to judge.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Coenzyme Q10
general_safety.short: Few adverse events were reported in trials. A case report describes reduced warfarin response while taking CoQ10.
